correctness.rationale: For exactly F3, every smooth projective geometrically connected genus-two curve has a smooth hyperelliptic model y²=F(X,Z) with F squarefree homogeneous degree six. With F3* squares={1}, arithmetic isomorphisms are exactly GL2(F3) binary-sextic substitutions; quotient by scalars ±I has order 24. Independently enumerated all 3^7 coefficient vectors, tested degree 5/6 and squarefree gcd to obtain 1,296 forms, formed 24 actions by binomial-coefficient expansion (not the package polynomial-power routine), partitioned into 69 disjoint complete orbits, and obtained Burnside fixed count 1,656=24·69. Factorization over F3, rank(A²) for A=[[c2,c1],[c5,c4]], and direct F3/F9 point counts yield exactly 19 nonempty (branch partition,3-rank) cells, 46 nonempty point-count triples, and the nineteen class/equation frequencies in RESULT.md. An independent F9 zeta-numerator computation verified rank(A²) for each of the 1,296 forms (rank-0:144, rank-1:288, rank-2:864 equation counts) and checks all 69 orbit representatives. The supplied full_joint.csv exactly agrees with census.json at all 46 rows. The six rank-zero arithmetic classes occur in (1,1,4),(1,2,3),(6), two each; unique orbit with four rational branch points is ordinary, has four F3-points, and six sextic forms. Stable Hasse-Witt rank, not naive rank(A), is used. The exhaustive finite proof covers all models because q and coefficient space are fixed; no inference to other field sizes is made.

value.rationale: The precisely motivated finite problem classifies simultaneously the Frobenius conjugacy class on the six Weierstrass points (2-torsion/branch geometry) and the Jacobian 3-rank (3-primary arithmetic) for all arithmetic genus-two classes over the smallest odd prime field. Neither 69 total classes nor 3,6,18 geometric rank marginals fixes the exact 19 intersection counts or the 46 class/point refinements; the supersingular placement and unique four-rational-branch-point ordinary class are specific nontrivial outputs. This complete small-field stratification and reproducible class representatives can support algorithm testing in genus-two arithmetic and finite-field moduli. Value is the natural exact joint invariant and exhaustive classification, not the raw 69 count, code presence alone, routine polynomial factorization or a claim of all-q generality.
